# Comparison for a 170 V / 2 W autonomous module

**Scope note:** I'm treating this as a design-review comparison, not a validated reference design. All three controllers can, in principle, be arranged for a flyback/boost-family topology producing ~170 V at ~2 W (≈12 mA) from either 10.8–13.2 V or 21.6–26.4 V. Nothing below should be read as "these are interchangeable." Any claimed equivalence is **not established** by public datasheet facts alone; bench verification at both line extremes and hot/cold is required.

---

## 1. Device-by-device facts and uncertainties

### LT3757A (with external 12 V gate drive)
- **Public facts:** Current-mode controller; wide VIN; programmable frequency; soft-start; internal LDO/BIAS arrangement with an external BIAS pin; UVLO/EN divider; COMP external compensation; slope compensation is internal/fixed per datasheet (verify exact value in your revision — **uncertain**).
- **External 12 V gate drive:** For a 10.8–13.2 V input this is nearly a pass-through; for 21.6–26.4 V it must be derived (LDO from VIN burns ~ (VIN−12)·Qgate·f; with a small FET at ~100 kHz this is a few mW–tens of mW — acceptable at 2 W but must be budgeted). **Pitfall:** the 12 V rail must be present and valid *before* or concurrently with controller enable, otherwise gate drive is undefined during startup. If 12 V is derived from the output or an auxiliary winding, you get a chicken-and-egg startup problem.
- **Uncertainty:** exact BIAS/LDO headroom behavior and whether the external 12 V can back-drive the BIAS pin within abs-max — check the specific datasheet revision.

### TPS40210 (external or direct drive)
- **Public facts:** Current-mode boost/flyback controller; VIN range covers both input classes; internal gate driver powered from VDD (typically ~8–12 V via an external VDD supply or bootstrap arrangement depending on configuration); programmable current limit via sense resistor; RC compensation on COMP; soft-start capacitor; slope compensation set by external resistor (Rsl).
- **Direct drive:** simplest, but gate-drive amplitude tracks VDD, so switching losses and EMI differ between 10.8 V and 26.4 V operation — verify FET Vgs margin and driver dissipation at the 26.4 V end.
- **Uncertainty:** VDD sourcing topology (external rail vs. bootstrap) materially changes startup; datasheet supports multiple arrangements — **do not assume** one is equivalent to another without matching your schematic.

### UCC28C43 (current-mode, industry-standard PWM)
- **Public facts:** Classic current-mode controller with UVLO thresholds set by the '43 variant; needs an external VCC (typically bootstrap/aux winding), external oscillator (RT/CT), external compensation, and external slope compensation (or relies on transformer/inductor ripple). No integrated high-side driver logic beyond a totem-pole output.
- **Pitfall:** the '43 UVLO/startup current and VCC clamp behavior define the minimum-line startup sequence; VCC must come from a startup path (resistor bleed or aux winding) — at 10.8 V minimum line with a high turns-ratio flyback, aux-winding startup can be marginal. **Uncertainty:** exact UVLO variant thresholds and startup current — confirm from the specific suffix datasheet.

---

## 2. Minimum-line startup pitfalls (all three)

- **UVLO divider tolerance:** At 10.8 V and 21.6 V minimums, resistor tolerance + comparator hysteresis + temperature drift can push effective startup above the specified minimum. Budget worst-case, not typical.
- **Aux-winding / bias bootstrap:** If VCC or 12 V bias comes from an aux winding, the converter must first start
